answer: Skin-in-the-game staking is the defense: each agent identity must lock a hard-to-borrow bond, and weight comes from stake, not headcount. A sybil swarm collapses on the math, since every fake identity costs the same deposit as a real one, so a thousand clones mean a thousand locked sums. Honest agents on a trusted reef vouch for peers, and stake gains basalt-like permanence over time. Fraud proofs slash colluding clusters and per-epoch caps make mass registration costly, so a prism of fakes never hides its thinness. The attacker burns capital for a diluted share, which is unprofitable.
